title.narrative: Enhanced national employment policy in the OPT

description.narrative: In the face of ongoing conflict in Gaza and its profound impacts on the socio-economic landscape of both Gaza and the West Bank, the labour market in Palestinian territories continues to confront grave challenges. The conflict's severity and persistence are poised to inflict long-term detriment on the Palestinian labour market, affecting the well-being of workers and their families through substantial job and income losses, and hindering access to education and training opportunities. The governance of the labour market by Palestinian institutions, including labour administration, social protection, public employment services, and social dialogue, is at risk of significant disruption due to the crisis. Most government institutions have adopted emergency response strategies that they are operating within, with all ministerial strategies submitted in October put on hold. Accordingly, the ILO will continue to implement targeted interventions supporting partners in OPT to have greater capacities to respond to labour market needs and challenges. The ILO created the Emergency Response Plan as a comprehensive proposal detailing interventions across three phases of relief, review, and recovery in response to and based on the decision made by the ILO Governing Body in November 2023. It also aligned ongoing work under the third Palestinian Decent Work Programme for OPT (2023–2025) to support the West Bank's resilience and stabilization. These four areas of activity capitalize on the ILO's comparative advantage in post-disaster labour market rehabilitation programs while addressing the new and pressing demands of the Palestinian labour market.
